summary: The `go` directive moves from 1.24.6 to 1.26.0. The plan lists only `tool` directives and the resulting require/go.sum changes for job 1. ci.yml reads `go-version-file: tui/go.mod`, so CI and every build of the TUI now use Go 1.26. That contradicts SC-1's 'build/vet/test unchanged' and the work order's out-of-scope line that no pinned version moves. The directive is probably forced by gitleaks v8.30.1, but neither the plan nor any record mentions it. The bump should be acknowledged in the work order or checked against what the gitleaks module actually requires.

The work order says none of the new requires link into the TUI binary, but the diff also raises modules the TUI already uses. golang.org/x/net goes 0.43.0 to 0.53.0, x/sync 0.16.0 to 0.20.0, x/sys 0.35.0 to 0.43.0 and x/text 0.28.0 to 0.36.0. Charmbracelet, bluemonday and termenv build on x/sys, x/text and x/net, so these shipped dependencies change as a side effect of adding the tools. The plan says the change moves where pins live, never what they pin. The existing `tests(tui)` check passed, but nothing else shows that the TUI's runtime behaviour is unchanged. This should be recorded as an accepted consequence, or the minimum-version selection checked.

SC-1 has no test in the diff or already on main. Its criteria (go tool staticcheck reports 0.8.1, go tool gitleaks runs, build unchanged) exist only as an observation command. The gate's `verified` record for job 1 lists only the existing checks and never invokes `go tool`, so it records nothing about the two tools. Jobs 2 and 3 exercise `go tool` indirectly, but job 1 alone proves the pin only by reading the `tool` and `require` lines.

SC-4 is named in job 4's delivers, but no test in the diff or on main exercises it. A grep for 'dependabot' outside docs/work found no file. The only check is the criterion's own python one-liner in plan.json, which is not part of verify.sh or any test. Nothing guards the allow list or group wiring against later edits (L216). The verified journal records were not read, and verify.sh was not read.

reason: Cannot deliver SC-1 without two consequences the work order does not record, and no code change in go.mod/go.sum can remove them. (1) `go 1.26.0` is required by honnef.co/go/tools v0.8.1 (go list -m GoVersion = 1.26.0; gitleaks v8.30.1 itself only requires 1.24.11), so CI's go-version-file now selects Go 1.26 for every build. (2) Minimum-version selection from the tools raised x/net 0.43.0->0.53.0, x/sync 0.16.0->0.20.0, x/sys 0.35.0->0.43.0, x/text 0.28.0->0.36.0; the TUI binary links x/net/html, x/sync/errgroup, x/sys/unix and x/text (go list -deps ./cmd/...), contradicting the work order's 'none of it links into the TUI binary'. The only alternative is dropping or lowering the staticcheck v0.8.1 pin, which changes what the job delivers. The operator must accept both consequences (and correct the work order's claim) or choose a different staticcheck pin. go.sum tidy correctness is checked: go mod verify reports all modules verified and a -mod=readonly build passes. SC-1 has no standing test by design of the plan; jobs 2 and 3 are where go tool is exercised.

summary: The test imports yaml, but PyYAML is not declared in daemon/pyproject.toml. It resolves only as a transitive entry in daemon/uv.lock (the lock lists pyyaml as a dependency of another package). If an upstream package drops it, collection fails with ImportError, and the gate reads that as a daemon test failure rather than a dependabot-config failure. The mypy override added at daemon/pyproject.toml line 103 widens the unchecked-import list to hide the missing stubs, so nothing flags the undeclared dependency. The tests themselves are sound: they assert the group, schedule, directories and allow list, and would go red if the allow list or group wiring changed. Fix would be declaring pyyaml in the daemon dev dependency group. I did not read the verified journal records or verify.sh, and I did not run the tests.
